objectives.description: Author tests/test-lake-build-guard.sh with 13 acceptance-mapped cases plus non-vacuousness section

approaches_tried.approach: Case 5/6 as originally drafted using genuine background-held flock contention to force the waiter branch
approaches_tried.reason: discovered during Phase 6 authoring that the sharing decision was scoped only to the waiter branch in cmd_build, which does not match Case 5's literal sequential (non-concurrent) test scenario in the plan; generalized decide_sharing() to run on lock acquisition regardless of contention (see deviations below), which let Case 5/6 be expressed as plain sequential invocations.

deviations.description: Phase 3's prose scopes the sharing decision to the waiter branch only ("On acquiring the lock as a waiter, read the record and apply the sharing decision").
deviations.reason: Case 5 (staleness) and Case 6 (abandoned lock) in Phase 6 are written as sequential, non-concurrent scenarios ("after A completes ... then run B"), which never enters the waiter branch under a waiter-only sharing check -- B would simply become a fresh, uncontended holder and always run a real build regardless of fingerprint/record state, making Cases 5 and 6 vacuous under the literal Phase 3 design. cmd_build was generalized so decide_sharing() is checked on lock acquisition unconditionally (both the immediate-acquire/uncontended path and the waiter/contended path), which is a strict superset of the original behavior: a freshly-started in_flight record (no prior complete build) still always falls through to a real build on the immediate-acquire path, so convoy-avoidance semantics for genuinely concurrent sessions (Case 4) are unchanged. This also makes sharing generally useful as a short-lived result cache for fully sequential repeat invocations, which is a net improvement over the narrower original scope.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- sharing decision now checked on lock acquisition unconditionally, not only the waiter branch; see phase-6-progress.json)*

deviations.description: compute_fingerprint()'s stat mode originally used stat -c '%n %s %Y' (whole-second mtime resolution).
deviations.reason: A same-size content edit landing within the same wall-clock second as the prior build produced an identical (path, size, mtime-in-seconds) tuple, causing decide_sharing() to spuriously treat a genuinely-changed tree as unchanged -- discovered while authoring Case 5's fixture (same-size edit, no artificial sleep). Switched to stat -c '%n %s %y' (nanosecond-resolution mtime) to close this gap for any filesystem that records sub-second mtimes (ext4/xfs/btrfs/tmpfs all do). The documented residual stat-mode edge narrows accordingly: now a restore/edit reproducing an identical size AND identical nanosecond-resolution mtime, rather than identical size and whole-second mtime.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- fingerprint stat mode now reads nanosecond-resolution mtime; see phase-6-progress.json)*
